subject: history_social
passage: For much of the twentieth century, the standard account held that the first people to reach the Americas walked south from Beringia through an ice-free corridor that opened between the two vast ice sheets covering what is now Canada. Archaeologist Ruth Calloway still regards that inland route as the most likely path, noting that it led directly to the grasslands of the interior, where herds of large game could have sustained migrating hunters.
passage_b: The inland route faces a problem of timing. Studies of ancient plant and animal remains suggest that the corridor could not have supported travelers until roughly 13,000 years ago, yet people were already living at Monte Verde, in southern Chile, more than a thousand years earlier. A coastal route, along shores rich in fish, shellfish, and seaweed, would have been open sooner and would have offered food the whole way.
stem: Based on the texts, how would the author of Text 2 most likely respond to the view held by Calloway in Text 1?

choices.A: By arguing that people reached South America before the inland route was usable
choices.B: By agreeing that the corridor opened early but denying that it offered enough large game
choices.C: By claiming that the first people to reach the Americas did not come from Beringia
choices.D: By suggesting that hunters on the interior grasslands later moved to the Pacific coast

explanation.why: Text 2's objection is "a problem of timing": the corridor could not support travelers until about 13,000 years ago, "yet people were already living at Monte Verde ... more than a thousand years earlier." If people were in Chile before the corridor was usable, they must have come another way. Text 2 uses that date to challenge Calloway's preferred route.
explanation.A: Correct. Text 2 notes that Monte Verde was occupied more than a thousand years before the corridor could support travelers.
explanation.B: Incorrect. Text 2 says the corridor could not support travelers until late, so it does not agree that it was usable early.
explanation.C: Incorrect. Text 2 offers a different route, not a different starting point; it never denies that people came from Beringia.
explanation.D: Incorrect. Text 2 says nothing about hunters moving from the grasslands to the coast.
